title: Multi-Objective Truss Optimization
prompt:
Design a planar Pratt truss bridge spanning 12 metres with the following requirements.

Loading:
- Dead load: 2 kN/m distributed along the top chord.
- Live load: 10 kN/m distributed along the bottom chord (applied at panel points).
- Load factors: 1.35 × dead + 1.5 × live (ultimate limit state).

Geometry:
- Span: 12 m, simply supported.
- Truss depth: 2 m (top chord to bottom chord).
- Number of panels: 6 (each panel 2 m wide).
- Pratt configuration: vertical members and diagonals sloping downward toward the centre.

Material:
- Steel: f_y = 355 MPa, E = 210,000 MPa.
- Members selected from standard circular hollow sections (CHS): 48.3×3.2, 60.3×3.2, 76.1×3.2, 88.9×4.0, 114.3×4.0, 139.7×5.0, 168.3×5.0 (diameter × wall thickness in mm).

Constraints (ALL must be satisfied simultaneously):

1. STRESS: Axial stress in every member ≤ f_y / γ_M0, where γ_M0 = 1.0. For members in compression, use the buckling resistance per EN 1993-1-1 with buckling curve 'a' (α = 0.21).
2. DEFLECTION: Maximum vertical deflection at midspan ≤ L/300 = 40 mm under unfactored service loads (1.0 × dead + 1.0 × live).
3. MINIMUM AREA: Every member must have a cross-sectional area ≥ 300 mm² (fabrication minimum).
4. TOTAL MASS: Minimize total steel mass. Report the mass.
5. SLENDERNESS: For compression members, the slenderness ratio L_member / r ≤ 200.
6. STATIC DETERMINACY: The truss must be statically determinate. Verify: m + r = 2j, where m = number of members, r = number of reactions, j = number of joints.

Your solution must include:

A. STRUCTURAL ANALYSIS:
1. Draw or describe the truss geometry (node coordinates).
2. Apply the factored loads at the appropriate panel points.
3. Solve for all member forces using the method of joints or method of sections. Show the calculation for at least 3 representative members (one top chord, one bottom chord, one diagonal).
4. Identify which members are in tension and which in compression.

B. MEMBER SIZING:
1. For each member, select the lightest CHS from the given list that satisfies the stress, buckling, and slenderness constraints.
2. For compression members, calculate the buckling resistance using:
   - Non-dimensional slenderness λ̄ = (L/r) × (1/π) × √(f_y/E)
   - Φ = 0.5 × [1 + α(λ̄ - 0.2) + λ̄²]
   - χ = 1 / [Φ + √(Φ² - λ̄²)]
   - N_b,Rd = χ × A × f_y
3. Present a member schedule table: member ID, length, force (kN), tension/compression, selected CHS, area, r (radius of gyration), slenderness, utilisation ratio.

C. DEFLECTION CHECK:
1. Calculate midspan deflection using the virtual work method (unit load method).
2. For each member: δ = Σ (F_i × f_i × L_i) / (A_i × E), where F_i is the real force (service loads), f_i is the virtual force (unit midspan load), L_i is member length, A_i is cross-sectional area.
3. Verify δ ≤ 40 mm.

D. SUMMARY TABLE:
Constraint | Required | Achieved | Pass/Fail
for all six constraints.
verification_method: Check: (1) Static determinacy: a 6-panel Pratt truss has 11 joints, 19 members, 3 reactions → 19 + 3 = 22 = 2 × 11 ✓. (2) Support reactions: total factored load = (1.35×2 + 1.5×10) × 12 = (2.7 + 15) × 12 = 212.4 kN, each reaction = 106.2 kN. (3) Maximum chord force is in the centre panel of the bottom chord ≈ 159.3 kN (tension). (4) Maximum compression is in the centre panel of the top chord ≈ -159.3 kN. (5) Diagonal forces decrease from supports to midspan. (6) Deflection calculation must use unfactored loads and account for all member deformations. (7) CHS selection must satisfy both stress and buckling for compression members.
why_frontier_hard: Three interacting calculations: member forces (analysis), section selection with buckling (design), and deflection check (serviceability). The virtual work deflection calculation is tedious and error-prone — it requires computing forces under two load cases (real and virtual), multiplying member by member, and summing. Models frequently: (1) forget to check buckling for compression members and size them on stress alone, (2) compute incorrect member forces (sign errors, forgetting that diagonals in a Pratt truss alternate tension/compression), (3) use the wrong load case for deflection (factored instead of unfactored), (4) select from the CHS list incorrectly (choosing sections that don't satisfy slenderness), (5) compute deflection wrong by omitting diagonal member contributions.
ground_truth_notes: 6-panel Pratt truss: 11 joints, 19 members, 3 reactions. Factored panel point loads: dead on top = 1.35×2×2 = 5.4 kN per joint (5 interior joints), live on bottom = 1.5×10×2 = 30 kN per joint (5 interior joints). Maximum bottom chord tension ≈ 159 kN in the central panel. Maximum top chord compression ≈ -159 kN. Maximum diagonal force ≈ 75 kN near supports. For the central top chord at 159 kN compression with a 2 m buckling length: CHS 88.9×4.0 (A = 1067 mm², r = 30.0 mm, λ = 67, λ̄ = 0.87, χ ≈ 0.74, N_b,Rd ≈ 280 kN > 159 kN) or lighter may work. Total mass typically 250-400 kg depending on optimization.
